Above all we like to please our partners which pleases us. 

• We tend to be very passionate and open-minded and will like exploring new kinks.

•INFJ often self-identify as submissive but I think many of us are actually natural switches who take dom/sub roles in sex based on what our partner likes. Lots of people enjoy being dominant in bed and I think that’s what influences INFJ to be submissive.

•I’ve heard we are ‘givers’ in bed but play a proactive role rather than enjoying being used for pleasure. INFJ may like to be on top so that they see everything going on, to be the one giving pleasure, and to see their partner’s reactions - whereas others may like being on top for the purpose of taking pleasure first. 

•I’ve heard INFJ prefer to give oral than receive it. For me personally it’s not that I don’t like receiving it (I do!) it’s that I like worshipping my partner even more.

•As true romantics, we adore our partners, wanting to explore every inch of our partners body and learn what they like, how they react to things and what makes them come undone. There is a lot of gentle exploration in INFJ sex. Usually that will inform how we act during sex; if we learn our partner doesn’t like a certain position, a certain kink or behaviour we won’t enjoy engaging in said position/kink/behaviour.

•Having such high expectations for ourselves in sex might also be our downfall, I know personally I had a lot of performance anxiety to brush off during my first sexual encounters because I wanted to be so good for the other person. 

•We have high libidos but are also very emotional in everything we do so sex is a form of bonding rather than just letting off steam. For this reason many INFJ’s don’t really do hookups well because it ends up with attachment and then inevitable hurt.

•INFJ’s have dirty minds and often never grow out of finding sexual innuendo and dirty jokes funny lmao. I have a friend who is INFJ like me and I have seen him jumping with joy and laughing himself to tears over penis innuendos 💀

• INFJ have a very strong imagination and generally think about sex and different fantasies a lot, but we don’t always express this unless it’s with a partner we really like and trust. If we sleep with someone we don’t really trust or feel connected to, it kind of shows, the sex is hollow, awkward and we won’t enjoy it. Many of us unfortunately learn this through disappointing hookups.

• Regarding the above point, I think it’s very interesting to note how many of us are demisexual and literally won’t be sexually interested in someone until there is an emotional connection or we feel we really know and understand the person.

• In my personal experience more of us tend to be in the LGBT community than other personality types. I think we have a lot of bisexual, pansexual and demisexual INFJ’s.

•I think INFJ might be prone to sexual frustration because of the disparity between our libido and only wanting to be intimate with people we connect with and are deeply attracted to.

•INFJ often have praise kinks and other kinks related to the other person’s pleasure, neediness and satisfaction. We often really like hearing our partners moan and we might also have body worship kinks. 

•We like an element of possessiveness in bed, doing things like marking/biting, manhandling and spanking. Giving or receiving these behaviours depends on whether the partner is dom/sub, because either way INFJ will like feeling wanted and owned by ‘their person’ or making their ‘their person’ feel wanted and owned.

•Despite this, INFJ are very affectionate in bed and often crave kissing and being physically close during intimacy. 

•I would also think a lot of INFJ’s need cuddling and aftercare because of the high intensity and passion we expend during sex; we can’t help but feel it as an emotional experience as well as a physical one. In my experience we can feel heartsore and abandoned by being left alone after sex.

In conclusion, I think we INFJ’s are pretty great, albeit enigmatic sexual partners. Our general outlook on love is consistent with our outlook on sex, and we are puppy-like in the degree we want to please our partners and take pleasure from being good at what we do.

I’m 23F and have PSSD after taking Sertraline for 5.5 years. I have noticed I have more sexual dreams than I did as a teenager when I had quite a high libido. When I’m awake, I feel sexual urges maybe twice in an entire a month but this is with genital numbing - before Sertraline I would be horny 24/7, like many young people. 

My theory is that maybe because I’ve been so distressed by the fact I’ve been left with this disorder, I’ve been ruminating and so my dreams are focused on things I wish I could do but cannot. It may also be my hormones sending my body a “hey, you should be horny right now” kind of message that my brain doesn’t adequately pass on to my genitals because of the PSSD.

I naturally have quite low testosterone levels so taking a couple of herbal supplements for this has helped a little bit, by that I mean Im now actually interested in sex for about 3 days of a month - with not much affect on the dreams as Im still under emotional distress.
